# 1. Load in libraries
```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(terra) # raster handling
library(tmap) # map making
library(stars)
```


# 2. Load in and prepare data
```{r}
#| message: false
#| results: hide

# Load night lights data (rasters)
# maybe use read_stars()
feb_7_h5 <- read_stars("data/VNP46A1/VNP46A1.A2021038.h08v05.001.2021039064328.tif")
feb_7_h6 <- read_stars("data/VNP46A1/VNP46A1.A2021038.h08v06.001.2021039064329.tif")
feb_16_h5 <- read_stars("data/VNP46A1/VNP46A1.A2021047.h08v05.001.2021048091106.tif")
feb_16_h6 <- read_stars("data/VNP46A1/VNP46A1.A2021047.h08v06.001.2021048091105.tif")

# Load roads data
# Query for just highways
roads_query <- "SELECT * FROM gis_osm_roads_free_1 WHERE fclass='motorway'"
# Reading in highways data
highways <- st_read("data/gis_osm_roads_free_1.gpkg", query=roads_query) # vector

# Load houses data
# Query for certain buildings
houses_query <- "SELECT *
FROM gis_osm_buildings_a_free_1
WHERE (type IS NULL AND name IS NULL)
OR type in ('residential', 'apartments', 'house', 'static_caravan', 'detached')"
# Reading in houses data
houses <- st_read("data/gis_osm_buildings_a_free_1.gpkg", query=houses_query) # vector
```

## Checking if CRSs match
```{r}
st_crs(highways) == st_crs(houses) # true
st_crs(feb_16_h6) == st_crs(houses)
st_crs(feb_16_h6) == st_crs(highways)
st_crs(feb_7_h6) == st_crs(houses)
st_crs(feb_7_h6) == st_crs(highways)
st_crs(feb_7_h6) == st_crs(feb_16_h6)
```


## Data Merging

Houston lies on the border of two tiles. We need to combine these two tiles together to get one raster for each date (2021-02-07 and 2021-02-16).

```{r}
houston_feb_7 <- st_mosaic(feb_7_h5, feb_7_h6)
houston_feb_16 <- st_mosaic(feb_16_h5, feb_16_h6)
```




## Comparing night light intensities before and after the first two storms

```{r}

# Crop to Houston area
houston_bbox <- st_bbox(c(
  xmin = -96.5,
  ymin = 29,
  xmax = -94.5,
  ymax = 30.5
), crs = st_crs(houston_feb_7))

pre_storm <- st_crop(houston_feb_7, houston_bbox)
post_storm <- st_crop(houston_feb_16, houston_bbox)

# Need to mask unrealistic values for mapping
masked_pre <- pre_storm
masked_pre[(masked_pre > 1000) | (masked_pre <= 0)] <- NA

masked_post <- post_storm
masked_post[(masked_post > 1000) | (masked_post <= 0)] <- NA

# Combine for side-by-side comparison
combined_crop <- c(masked_pre, masked_post)
names(combined_crop) <- c("February 7, 2021 (Before)", "February 16, 2021 (After)")
```

```{r}
tm_shape(combined_crop) +
   tm_raster(
    col.legend = tm_legend(title = "Light Intensity (nW cm⁻² sr⁻¹)"),
    col.scale = tm_scale(values = "inferno")
  ) +
    tm_facets(ncol = 2, free.scales = FALSE) +
    tm_title("Houston Night Lights Before and After the Storm") +
    tm_layout(legend.outside = TRUE,
              legend.outside.position = "right",
              legend.outside.size = 0.12,
              panel.labels = c("February 7 (Before)", "February 16 (After)")
  ) +
    tm_graticules(lwd = 0.4, col = "white", alpha = 0.3, labels.size = 0.5, n.x = 5, n.y = 5)
```




## Create blackout mask

To identify places that experienced a blackout, we need to create a “mask” that indicates for each cell whether or not it experienced a blackout.

```{r}
# Find the change in night lights intensity caused by the storm
night_light_diff <- rast(houston_feb_7) - rast(houston_feb_16)

# Reclassify the difference raster, assuming that any location that experienced a drop of more than 200 nW cm^-2 sr^-1 experienced a blackout

# Create reclassification matrix
rcl <- matrix(c(
          -Inf, 200, 0, # 0 means no blackout
          200, Inf, 1 # 1 means blackout
          ),
          ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE)

# Use reclassification to reclassify elevation
reclass_lights <- classify(night_light_diff, rcl = rcl)
summary(reclass_lights)

# Assign NA to locations without blackouts
blackout_mask <- ifel(reclass_lights == 0, NA, 1)

# Convert raster to polygons
blackout_mask_vect <- as.polygons(blackout_mask, na.rm = TRUE)

# Convert polygons to sf
blackout_mask_vect <- st_as_sf(blackout_mask_vect)

# Making geometries valid
houston_blackout <- st_make_valid(
  st_crop(blackout_mask_vect, houston_bbox)
)

# Re-projecting blackout to EPSG:3083
houston_reproject <- st_transform(houston_blackout, crs = "EPSG:3083")

```


## Exclude highways from the cropped blackout mask

Highways may have experienced changes in their night light intensities that are unrelated to the storm. Therefore, we should excluded any locations within 200 meters of all highways in the Houston area.

```{r}
# Transforming CRS to match
highways <- st_transform(highways, crs = "EPSG:3083")

# Creating a 200m buffer
highways_buffer <- highways |> 
  st_union() |> 
  st_buffer(dist = 200)

# Excluding highways
blackout_no_highways <- st_difference(houston_reproject, highways_buffer)
```


## Identify the number of homes likely impacted by blackouts
```{r}

### TAKES AWHILE TO RUN

houses <- st_transform(houses, crs = "EPSG:3083")

blackout_houses <- houses |> 
  st_filter(blackout_no_highways)

n_blackout_houses <- nrow(blackout_houses) # 157408 houses
```

There were 157,408 houses that were likely impacted by the blackouts.
